aiSummary.oneLiner: High-performance WebSocket proxy for Telegram MTProto connections.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Tgwsproxy acts as a specialized intermediary, wrapping Telegram's proprietary MTProto protocol inside standard WebSocket connections. It enables web-based Telegram clients to communicate directly with Telegram's backend servers without relying on intermediary HTTP polling or third-party APIs. The proxy is built in Rust for maximum concurrency and minimal memory footprint, efficiently handling thousands of simultaneous user connections. This infrastructure is critical for developers building responsive, browser-based Telegram clients or bots.
keyFeatures: Protocol wrapping: Encapsulates MTProto binary streams securely within standard WebSocket frames.
High concurrency: Built in Rust using asynchronous I/O to handle thousands of simultaneous connections.
Low latency: Minimizes overhead to provide near real-time messaging performance for web clients.
Secure termination: Handles TLS termination efficiently before forwarding traffic to Telegram datacenters.
Resource efficient: Maintains a minimal memory footprint even under heavy sustained load.

useCases.title: Web client infrastructure
useCases.description: Deploy the proxy to serve as the backend connection layer for a custom browser-based Telegram client.

useCases.title: Network restriction bypass
useCases.description: Route Telegram traffic through standard WebSockets to bypass restrictive corporate firewalls.

useCases.title: Bot hosting
useCases.description: Provide a reliable, high-performance connection layer for web-hosted Telegram automation bots.

useCases.title: Protocol translation
useCases.description: Translate legacy TCP MTProto traffic into WebSockets for integration with modern edge networks.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Backend engineers and developers building web-based Telegram clients or infrastructure. It requires experience with Rust, WebSockets, and network proxy deployment.
